question.text: An institutional investor wants to use a Cat III AIF for ALPHA generation. This implies:

answer.text: Active management aiming to outperform benchmarks with skill-based strategies

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines alpha as excess return over a benchmark and explains that active management attempts to outperform the benchmark by identifying mispriced securities. An investor allocating to a Cat III AIF for alpha is therefore buying skill-based active management, not passive exposure. The Trap: Passive index tracking by definition targets beta, not alpha. Risk-free or dividend-only strategies do not aim to outperform a benchmark through security selection and so do not match the workbook's definition of alpha generation. Note: The alpha-as-excess-return-over-benchmark and active-management definitions are taken from the AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook (Series XIX-B).
